items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree a large prisoner exchange
items.summary: US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended with Russia and Ukraine agreeing a large exchange of prisoners of war, described as the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022. The talks produced no wider breakthrough.
items.why: Even partial progress shifts the outlook for energy prices and European business confidence.

items.title: Trump says the US does not need a deal with Iran
items.summary: President Trump said on Thursday that 'we don't need a deal with Iran' while acknowledging the conflict is not over, CBS reports. Iran's Assembly of Experts has urged the leadership to consider leaving the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
items.why: Tension around Iran drives oil prices, which feed straight into India's inflation and company costs.

items.title: COP31 leaders' summit ends with electrification pledges
items.summary: The two-day leaders' segment in Antalya closed on 12 November with more countries endorsing the presidency's 35x35 electrification pledge and new philanthropic money for the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, the World Resources Institute says. There was no single negotiated declaration; talks run to 20 November.
items.why: Electrification targets shape green-skills demand and the sustainability claims brands can make.

items.title: Over $480 million pledged for methane action at COP31
items.summary: Philanthropic partners committed more than US$480 million for methane and other super pollutants at COP31, and a further US$25 million will extend a country action programme to seven more countries, the Climate and Clean Air Coalition reports.
items.why: Shows how private money is filling gaps in climate finance, a growing area for CSR and ESG roles.

items.title: Big names skip COP31: no Trump, Xi or leaders of France, Germany and Italy
items.summary: The US and Chinese presidents did not attend the Antalya summit, with China sending Vice-President Han Zheng, and several large EU economies were absent although Ursula von der Leyen attended. Reports of how many leaders came vary between about 90 and 100.
items.why: Who shows up signals how much weight governments will put behind climate rules that companies must follow.

items.title: Retail inflation hits 6.09%, above the RBI's ceiling
items.summary: October CPI inflation rose to 6.09% from 5.54% in September, the first breach of the RBI's 6% upper limit in two years and above a Reuters poll forecast of 5.93%. Rural inflation was 6.63% and urban 5.41%.
items.why: Higher prices squeeze household budgets and salary planning, and change how brands price and promote.

items.title: Odds of a December repo rate hike rise
items.summary: With inflation above the tolerance band, economists now see a higher chance of the RBI raising the repo rate at its December meeting, ThePrint reports. Food inflation was the main driver; sources differ on the exact food figure (8.51% to 8.94%), so treat it as provisional.
items.why: A rate hike raises loan costs for companies and consumers, cooling hiring and big-ticket demand.

items.title: Onion prices more than double year on year
items.summary: Onion prices were up 116.22% in October against 108.13% in September, and the all-India index rose 0.51% month on month, according to coverage of the official release.
items.why: Food-price spikes hit FMCG volumes first, a live example for consumer behaviour and pricing.

items.title: Cabinet clears Rs 3,230 crore national museum in North and South Block
items.summary: A current-affairs digest dated 12 November reports Cabinet approval for the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in North and South Block at Rs 3,230 crore, and a ban on exporting lithium-ion battery 'black mass' to support domestic recycling. Not yet checked against an official release.
items.why: Battery recycling policy creates a new domestic industry with its own talent and supply-chain needs.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty end flat after a volatile session
items.summary: The Sensex closed at 81,911.01, up 0.04%, and the Nifty at 25,299.35, up 0.18%, on 12 November. Realty led with a gain of about 4% while autos fell about 1%, and mid and small caps outperformed.
items.why: A pause after a strong month, on the day inflation data landed; watch rate-sensitive sectors.

items.title: easyJet shareholders approve Apollo's £5.7 billion takeover
items.summary: More than 97% of scheme shares backed Apollo's proposed £5.7 billion acquisition of easyJet. The deal is expected to complete before the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to remaining conditions.
items.why: Private-equity ownership usually brings restructuring, a classic HR transformation scenario.

items.title: Nebius revenue jumps 571% but guidance is trimmed
items.summary: AI cloud firm Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571%, while moving its 2026 revenue guidance to the low end of its range and raising planned capital spending to about $27 billion, an earnings digest reports.
items.why: Shows the scale of AI infrastructure spending and the pressure to turn it into revenue.

items.title: Spectrum Brands plans to buy Helen of Troy
items.summary: Spectrum Brands said on its fourth-quarter earnings call that it plans to acquire Helen of Troy through its Empower Brands subsidiary.
items.why: A consumer-brands merger means portfolio and brand-architecture decisions, core marketing strategy work.

items.title: Nvidia shares fall 14% as CEO Jensen Huang is reported to resign
items.summary: Nvidia fell about 14% at Thursday's open after reports that Jensen Huang resigned, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO, according to CNBC's market coverage and reports relayed by Techmeme. Some digests describe it differently, so details are provisional.
items.why: A sudden CEO exit at the world's most valuable chipmaker is a live case in succession planning and governance.

items.title: US weighs AI chip export licences for seven countries
items.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering export licences for controlled AI chips going into data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Norway, Brazil and South Africa, with an announcement possible this month.
items.why: Where AI chips can go decides where data-centre jobs and investment land.

items.title: Taiwan proposes protecting 46 key technologies
items.summary: Taiwan's National Science and Technology Council has proposed widening its list of national core key technologies from 42 to 46 items. The draft is still in public consultation.
items.why: Technology-protection rules limit talent moves and partnerships in the chip industry.

items.title: Budget phone makers turn to recycled memory as costs surge
items.summary: Rising memory prices are pushing low-end smartphone makers towards recycled memory, while Samsung leans on its scale. Counterpoint Research says memory and storage now make up as much as 54% of component costs in ultra-low-end models.
items.why: Component costs decide entry-level phone prices in India, a key mass-market category.

items.title: South Korea plans eight homegrown on-device AI chips by 2030
items.summary: South Korea's industry ministry unveiled a roadmap on 12 November for eight domestic AI chips and two chip-design IP assets by 2030.
items.why: Government-led chip plans create specialised hiring drives and public-private partnerships.

items.title: Anthropic's IPO order book reported several times oversubscribed
items.summary: An AI news digest says Anthropic's IPO order book is running several times oversubscribed ahead of pricing next week, and that TSMC's board approved up to $1 billion of AI investments, part of it in Anthropic shares. Aggregator report, not yet confirmed by a primary source.
items.why: The largest AI listing will set the tone for tech valuations and hiring budgets.

items.title: Google ships a Gemini 'Decisions' API for rapid yes-or-no answers
items.summary: Google released the Gemini Decisions API, built to answer up to 1,000 yes-or-no or multiple-choice questions in about a quarter of a second, an AI digest reports.
items.why: Fast bulk classification is the kind of tool that automates screening and tagging work in HR and marketing.

items.title: RBI's inflation band is 2% to 6%
items.summary: The RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%; October's 6.09% is the first reading above it since October 2024 (6.21%).
items.why: A number worth knowing for any economy question in an interview.

items.title: Indian benchmarks are up over 10% this month
items.summary: The Nifty 50 and Sensex had delivered more than 10% month to date as of 12 November.
items.why: Context for how strong November has been for markets.

items.title: Global fossil-fuel emissions were broadly flat in 2026
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told COP31 that global fossil fuel carbon emissions remained broadly stable in 2026.
items.why: A useful data point for sustainability discussions.
